title: Savings Signal Lanes: Initiative Tracker for Granular Cost Controls (batching / caching / quantization)
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Runbook-style initiative to create maintainable 'signal lanes' that connect observed traffic patterns to automated serving controls (batching policies, prefix/KV cache heuristics, and quantization profiles). The outcome should be a repeatable lifecycle for experiments -> safe rollout -> cost capture where product can declaratively tune savings per route, customer tier, and SLA.
goals: Define signal taxonomy (latency-sensitive vs throughput-oriented requests) and map to control lanes
Ship an initial set of lane-aware runtime flags (3 lanes) and console controls for PM/ops to tune per-lane budgets
Run 8 field experiments across customer segments to validate >=15% token-cost reduction without >5% latency SLO regressions
Create monitoring dashboards and an attribution model that ties dollar savings to config changes
success_metrics: Token cost reduction attributable to lanes >= 15% for non-latency-critical traffic
No more than 5% of requests in latency-sensitive lane exceeding p95 baseline
Experiment-to-rollout time reduced from 8 weeks to 3 weeks
Automated rollbacks triggered and executed < 30 minutes when regressions detected
milestones: M3: Console lane UI and cost dashboards (DES/PM) (2025-04-05)
M4: First field trials (4 experiments, small cohort) (2025-04-30)
M5: Attribution model & automated rollback flow (2025-05-20)
M6: Rollout to Dedicated customers as opt-in (2025-06-20)
current_blockers: ENG: Kernel-level batching knobs timing conflicts with autoscaler (ENG-2310) - mitigation plan in PR #782
Design: lane UI copy needs legal review for opt-in language
Observability: need trace-level cost attribution for cached vs non-cached tokens
recent_activity: 2025-02-04: Kickoff sync with Eng, Design, Observability teams. Agreed on three initial lanes: latency-critical, standard, prefetch-friendly.
2025-02-18: Eng spike completed - submitted RFC 'lane-aware batching' (RFC-2025-02) and linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/761
2025-02-25: PM/Design usability session for Console controls; initial mockups in Figma https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/signal-lanes
2025-03-03: Observability prototype emits lane tags in traces; dashboard template created in Grafana https://grafana.redwood.company/d/signal-lanes
2025-03-10: Runtime prototype deployed to staging with toggle flags; small synthetic benchmark shows 12% token cost reduction on prefetch workload
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-02-20: Start with 3 lanes rather than a continuous score — simpler rollouts and easier reasonability for customers
Decision 2025-03-05: Use prefix-based KV cache tagging as first-class lane signal instead of heuristic-only approach
Trade-off: aggressive quantization policies will be limited to standard and prefetch lanes to avoid hallucination risk in latency-critical lane
risks_mitigation: Risk: Model quality regressions from quantization. Mitigation: gate quantization experiments behind automated quality checks tied to eval prompt sets.
Risk: Customer confusion about opt-in changes. Mitigation: add explicit per-organization UI consent and email notifications for Dedicated customers.
Risk: Savings attribution in multi-stage pipelines. Mitigation: instrument token-level provenance and run A/B attribution with sampling
